detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876) with the modular input for `aws:vpcflow`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `src` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable vpc integration in AWS and forward findings/logs via `Splunk_TA_aws` into `index=aws` with `sourcetype=aws:vpcflow`. Validate field extractions before alerting.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:vpcflow" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:vpcflow" action=REJECT
| table _time src dest src_port dest_port action bytes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.153_vpc_flow_log_rejected_co_153"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:vpcflow` in `index=aws` to detect vpc flow log rejected connections spike. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon VPC console Flow logs for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `src` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_153_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Notable-style table, severity timeline, single-value open finding count..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Add-on for AWS (`Splunk_TA_aws`, Splunkbase 1876) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
